reference.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology / Kandel's Principles of Neural Science
clinicalPearls: Rods mediate scotopic dim-light vision (high sensitivity, low acuity); cones mediate photopic daylight trichromatic vision (fovea)
In darkness, high cGMP levels hold cyclic nucleotide-gated channels open (dark current), maintaining tonic depolarization (-40 mV) and glutamate release
Light activates rhodopsin (11-cis to all-trans retinal) -> metarhodopsin II activates transducin -> cGMP phosphodiesterase hydrolyzes cGMP
Channel closure causes photoreceptor hyperpolarization (-70 mV), DECREASING glutamate release onto bipolar cells
On-center bipolar cells express mGluR6 receptors and DEPOLARIZE to light; off-center bipolar cells express AMPA receptors and hyperpolarize
reference.pathophysiology: Genetic mutations in rhodopsin or photoreceptor disc turnover cause retinitis pigmentosa, characterized by progressive rod apoptosis, bone-spicule retinal pigmentation, nyctalopia (night blindness) and tunnel vision. Congenital stationary night blindness and achromatopsia arise from transducin, phosphodiesterase or cyclic nucleotide channel subunit defects.
additionalInvestigations: Full-field electroretinography (ERG) assessing scotopic and photopic retinal responses
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) of macula measuring photoreceptor layer integrity
